d1: The node’s binary criterion is too narrow for the task rubric: it verifies that a mug is right of the headphones, but the edited image contains multiple mugs and appears to leave the original blue mug as a blurred remnant while adding mugs and altering the headphones. Thus a right-side mug can satisfy this check even when the requested edit is only partially fulfilled. Refine the binding/criterion to identify the mug corresponding to the source object and assess its change relative to the source, while preserving uncertainty when identity or edit evidence is unclear. Do not infer completion from the rightmost mug alone; the aggregate partial label is a constraint, not atomic ground truth. The five high-confidence yes traces consistently support the relative-position observation, so investigate criterion/binding and partial-progress coverage rather than treating this as a visual failure or lowering confidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported.
